spec.cue: Hold still, as a jumping spider watches. Only what moves catches its eyes.

fov.note: the secondary eye pairs together, near 360 degrees

topoA.note: the principal eyes are sharper in the middle of their strip; the app's choice

fovea.note: the app's choice; no magnification ratio is recorded

sat.note: two colour classes in the principal eyes, so less than full colour

gain.note: the app's choice for dim light

gate.note: the app's choice: still things fade in the side eyes

rate.note: the app's pace; the flicker records give a fusion limit of about 40 Hz, which does not fix this value

living.note: no record gives extra weight for living movement

uvBlue.note: the camera's blue stands in for ultraviolet

sweep.note: a sweep of at least 2 degrees, with a cycle of 1.1 to 1.3 s

examine.note: the app's choice of how long a target is looked over

ior.note: the app's choice; the record R386 says habituation to a place is tied to location and lasts hours

rows: The principal eyes that look forward see two colour classes, ultraviolet and green. Colours are told apart in a way close to a dichromat.
The front eyes resolve fine detail in a narrow upright strip about 2 degrees wide and 21 degrees high. The rest of the picture is blurred.
A wide view from the side eyes
Four side eyes cover close to the full circle and respond to movement. Still things fade from the picture, so what moves stands out.
The front eyes move a strip across the scene, scanning side to side about once every 1.2 seconds and turning back and forth as they go.
The brightness, sharpness falloff, glow colour, pace, pull of the gaze and the ultraviolet stand-in are the app's guesses, since no record gives them for this animal.
